title: Your Home and the Rooms in It
overview:
Say where you live.
Name the rooms in a home.
Say what there is in each room.
Say my home and our home.
functions: Name the rooms in a home
Say what there is in a room
Ask a person where they live
Say my and our about a place
Say a place is clean or not
learningPath: Patterns: I live in, and there is a kitchen.
Write four lines about where you live.
Practice and quiz. Check your answers.
lectureScript:
This is Unit 12. Where do you live?
First, two words. House and flat.
A house is a whole building.
A flat is part of a building.
And home is where you live, house or flat.
Say them with me. House. Flat. Home.
Now, I live in.
I live in a flat.
I live in a small house.
Say it with me. I live in.
Now the rooms.
The kitchen. You cook there.
The bedroom. You sleep there.
The bathroom. You wash there.
And the toilet.
Say them with me. Kitchen. Bedroom. Bathroom. Toilet.
Some homes have a garden. Some have stairs.
Now we use a pattern from Unit 8.
There is a kitchen.
There are two bedrooms.
Remember: one thing is, more than one are.
Last, my and our.
I live alone: my flat.
I live with people: our flat.
Say them with me. My flat. Our flat.
That is Unit 12. Go and describe your home.

grammar.title: I live in
grammar.explanation:
Two small words say where your home is.
Live always takes in for a place.
grammar.rule:
I live in a flat.
I live in a small house.
I live in London.

he, she, it → lives
She lives in a house.

Question: Where do you live?
grammar.workedExample:
Your home is a flat.
1. Start: I live.
2. Then in.
3. Then a flat.
4. Say: I live in a flat.
5. Add more: I live in a small flat.
grammar.mistake:
No: I live a flat.
English needs in.
Yes: I live in a flat.
grammar.tip: Live takes in for a place.
grammar.practice:
Finish each one.
1. I ___ ___ a flat.
2. She ___ ___ a house.
3. Where do you ___?
4. They ___ ___ a big house.
grammar.answers:
1. live in
2. lives in
3. live
4. live in
All four? She and he take lives, with an s.

grammar.title: There is a kitchen
grammar.explanation:
This is the pattern from Unit 8, on new ground.
One room: there is. More rooms: there are.
grammar.rule:
There is a kitchen.
There are two bedrooms.
There is a garden.
There are no stairs.

Question: Is there a garden?
          Are there two bedrooms?
grammar.workedExample:
Your flat has one kitchen and two bedrooms.
1. One kitchen, so there is.
2. Say: There is a kitchen.
3. Two bedrooms, so there are.
4. Say: There are two bedrooms.
5. Join them with and, in one line.
grammar.mistake:
Do not use it has for a room list.
It works, but there is sounds more natural here.
grammar.tip: One room: is. More rooms: are.
grammar.practice:
Write is or are.
1. There ___ a kitchen.
2. There ___ three rooms.
3. There ___ no garden.
4. There ___ two windows.
5. There ___ a bathroom.
6. There ___ four beds.
grammar.answers:
1. is
2. are
3. is
4. are
5. is
6. are
Five or six right? Good.

grammar.title: Where do you live?
grammar.explanation: One question, and a short answer is enough.
grammar.rule:
Where do you live?
In a flat.
I live in a flat.

Do you live alone?
No, with my family.

Is it near here?
Yes, it is near the school.
grammar.workedExample:
Somebody asks where your home is.
1. A short answer is fine: In a flat.
2. A longer one: I live in a small flat.
3. They may ask: Alone?
4. Answer: No, with my family.
5. Two or three short lines is a real conversation.
grammar.mistake:
Do not say: Where you live?
English needs do in this question.
Yes: Where do you live?
grammar.practice:
Ask and answer.
1. Where do you live?
2. Do you live alone?
3. Is it near here?
4. How many rooms are there?
grammar.answers:
Any true answer is right.
Check: did you answer in a short sentence, not one word?
Did the question in 1 keep the word do?

grammar.title: My and our
grammar.explanation:
My is for you alone.
Our is for you and other people.
grammar.rule:
I live alone:        my flat, my kitchen
I live with people:  our flat, our kitchen

my  →  I
our →  we

This is my bedroom. That is our kitchen.
grammar.workedExample:
You share a flat with two people.
1. The flat belongs to all of you.
2. So use our: our flat.
3. But your bedroom is only yours.
4. So use my: my bedroom.
5. In one line: my bedroom in our flat.
grammar.mistake:
Do not use our when you live alone.
It tells the listener something untrue.
grammar.tip: My is one person. Our is more.
grammar.practice:
Write my or our.
1. I live alone. This is ___ flat.
2. We live together. This is ___ kitchen.
3. Only I sleep here. This is ___ bedroom.
4. We all use it. This is ___ bathroom.
5. I live with my family. This is ___ home.
grammar.answers:
1. my
2. our
3. my
4. our
5. our
Four or five right? Good.

readings.title: My Flat
readings.setting: A small flat on the second floor
readings.passage:
I live in a small flat.
It is on the second floor.
There are three rooms.
There is a kitchen and a bathroom.
There are two bedrooms.
There is no garden.
My bedroom is little but it is clean.
The kitchen has a window.
I like it here.

readings.title: Where Do You Live?
readings.setting: Outside a school, after a class
readings.passage:
Where do you live?
In a flat, near the station.
Is it big?
No, it is little. Two bedrooms.
Do you live alone?
No. I live with my sister.
Is there a garden?
No, but there is a window.
That is enough.

readings.title: For People in This Building
readings.setting: A wall by the front door of a block of flats
readings.passage:
Keep the stairs clean.
Do not put bags in the hall.
The water tap in the garden is for everyone.
A problem in your flat? Tell the desk.
The desk is on the first floor.

comprehension.q: What kind of home is it?
comprehension.why: Line 1: I live in a small flat.
Line 2: It is on the second floor.

comprehension.q: Does the person like the flat?
comprehension.why: The last line: I like it here.
Line 2: In a flat, near the station.
Line 6: I live with my sister.
Line 8: No, but there is a window.
The last line of the notice.

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — Where I live
speaking.instructions:
Say four lines about your home.
1. I live in a ___.
2. It is ___ (big, little, near the school).
3. There are ___ rooms.
4. I live ___ (alone, with my family).
Tap the mic. Say the four lines.
Check: did you say live in, not just live?
speaking.tutor: Tell the tutor where you live. Ask where it lives.
speaking.instructionsSpeech:
Say four lines about your home.
One. I live in a ...
Two. It is ... big, little, near the school.
Three. There are ... rooms.
Four. I live ... alone, with my family.
Tap the mic. Say the four lines.
Check: did you say live in, not just live?

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — There is, there are
speaking.instructions:
Say six lines about your home.
1. There is a kitchen.
2. There is a ___.
3. There are two ___.
4. There are ___ rooms.
5. There is no ___.
6. There are no ___.
Tap the mic. Say the six lines.
Check: is for one, are for many?
speaking.tutor: Describe your home to the tutor. Use there is and there are.
speaking.instructionsSpeech:
Say six lines about your home.
One. There is a kitchen.
Two. There is a ...
Three. There are two ...
Four. There are ... rooms.
Five. There is no ...
Six. There are no ...
Tap the mic. Say the six lines.
Check: is for one, are for many?

speaking.title: Speaking 3 — Ask about a home
speaking.instructions:
Read A. Say B.
1. A: Where do you live? B: In a flat, near the station.
2. A: Is it big? B: No, it is little.
3. A: Do you live alone? B: No, with my sister.
4. A: Is there a garden? B: No, but there is a window.
Tap the mic. Say the four B lines.
Check: short answers, not one word?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor three questions about a home. Answer its questions too.

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — Name the rooms
speaking.instructions:
Tap Listen. Name the room.
1. You cook there.
2. You sleep there.
3. You wash there.
4. It is outside, with plants.
5. They take you up a floor.
6. The small room with a toilet.
Tap the mic. Say six answers.
Check: kitchen, bedroom, bathroom, garden, stairs, toilet.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor what you do in each room of a home.

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — Where is the toilet?
speaking.instructions:
This is a question you will need. Say it well.
1. Excuse me. Where is the toilet, please?
2. Sorry? Again, please.
3. Up the stairs? Thank you.
4. Is it on the left or the right?
Tap the mic. Say all four.
Check: did you say excuse me first?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor where the toilet is. Then check the answer back.

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — The th in bathroom
speaking.instructions:
Listen and repeat.
bathroom ... three ... think ... thin
This th has no buzz. Just air.
It is not t and it is not s.
Now say these lines.
The bathroom is clean.
There are three rooms.
Tap the mic. Say both lines.
Check: air, not a buzz, in bathroom?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to say bathroom and batroom. Say which is right.

writing.title: Writing 1 — Where I live
writing.prompt:
Write four lines about your home.
Use I live in and there is or there are.
writing.model:
I live in a small flat.
It is on the second floor.
There are three rooms.
There is no garden.
writing.criteria:
Four lines.
I live in is in the first one.
There is or there are is in two of them.
Each line ends with a full stop.
writing.extension: Add a line about which room you like best.

writing.title: Writing 2 — One room
writing.prompt:
Choose one room in your home.
Write four lines about it.
Say what there is, and where things are.
writing.model:
My bedroom is little.
There is a bed by the window.
There is a little table.
My bag is under the bed.
writing.criteria:
Four lines about one room.
There is or there are in two of them.
At least one line says where a thing is.
writing.extension: Add a line saying what there is NOT in the room.

activities.answers:

Five or six right: good.

activities.instructions:
Write is or are.
1. There ___ a kitchen.
2. There ___ three rooms.
3. There ___ no garden.
4. There ___ two windows.
5. There ___ a bathroom.
6. There ___ four beds.
activities.answers:

2. are
3. is
4. are
5. is

Five or six right: good.

activities.title: Practice 3 — House or flat?
activities.instructions:
Write house or flat.
1. A whole building. ___
2. Part of a building. ___
3. It often has a garden. ___
4. It is on the third floor. ___
5. It has its own front door to the street. ___
activities.answers:
1. house
2. flat
3. house
4. flat
5. house
Four or five right: good. A flat is inside a bigger building.

activities.title: Practice 4 — My or our?
activities.instructions:
Write my or our.
1. I live alone. This is ___ flat.
2. We live together. This is ___ kitchen.
3. Only I sleep here. This is ___ bedroom.
4. We all use it. This is ___ bathroom.
5. I live with my family. This is ___ home.
activities.answers:
1. my
2. our
3. my
4. our
5. our
Four or five right: good.

activities.title: Practice 5 — Live or lives?
activities.instructions:
Write live or lives.
1. I ___ in a flat.
2. She ___ in a house.
3. We ___ together.
4. He ___ near here.
5. They ___ in a big house.
6. Where do you ___?
activities.answers:
1. live
2. lives
3. live
4. lives
5. live
6. live
Five or six right: good. He and she take lives.

activities.title: Practice 6 — Read the notice
activities.instructions:
Read For People in This Building again.
1. What must you keep clean?
2. What must you not put in the hall?
3. Who can use the water tap?
4. Where do you go with a problem?
5. What floor is the desk on?
activities.answers:
1. The stairs
2. Bags
3. Everyone
4. The desk
5. The first floor
Four or five right: you can read a building notice.
activities.solo: Read it, then answer without looking.

quizzes.q: A whole building where people live is a ___.
quizzes.why: A flat is part of a building. A house is the whole thing.
I takes live. He and she take lives.
The kitchen is where you cook.
The bedroom is where you sleep.

quizzes.q: They take you up to another floor. They are the ___.
There ___ a kitchen in my flat.
Which question asks about a home?

quizzes.why: This question needs do before you.

quizzes.q: You live alone. This is ___ flat.
quizzes.why: My is for one person. Our is for more.

quizzes.q: You live with two people. This is ___ kitchen.
quizzes.why: Our is for a place you share.

quizzes.q: Water comes out of it. It is a ___.
quizzes.why: You turn a water tap and water comes out.

teacherNotes.note: Every pattern card has a worked example, every practice has a key, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back, check.

teacherNotes.type: The first real spiral in the level
teacherNotes.note: There is and there are was taught in Unit 8 with objects and comes back here with rooms. Say that out loud: the learner should notice they already know the pattern. That recognition is worth more than the rooms.

teacherNotes.type: Housing is not a neutral topic
teacherNotes.note: Some learners are in temporary or shared accommodation they would rather not describe. Let a learner answer at whatever level of detail they choose, accept in a flat as a complete answer, and never push for the number of people.

teacherNotes.type: Where is the toilet is a real-world question
teacherNotes.note: Speaking 5 exists for that one sentence. A learner should leave this unit able to say it without hesitating, including the excuse me at the front.

teacherNotes.type: House and flat are not interchangeable
teacherNotes.note: Learners often use house for any home. It is understood, but a flat on the third floor is not a house and the distinction matters on forms and to landlords.

assignment.title: My home
assignment.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Record yourself. Say four lines about where you live.
Use I live in and there is or there are.
2. Write four lines about one room in your home.
Say what there is and where things are.
Listen back before you finish.
assignment.submissionType: Audio recording and a written page
